Forbes: Why Every Industry Is Becoming A Semiconductor Industry


# Forbes: Why Every Industry Is Becoming A Semiconductor Industry


- Oct 20, 2026


- Michal Siwinski


-


< 1


min read


Most companies will never design a chip, yet advances in semiconductor technology increasingly determine what they can build, how they innovate and how they compete.


For decades, semiconductors were treated as a specialized technology domain, essential building blocks that were largely invisible to anyone outside engineering and technology teams. For most other executives, the semiconductor layer was easy to ignore. Today, the technologies shaping modern business—from AI and automation to connected products and intelligent infrastructure—are all built on a foundation of increasingly sophisticated silicon.


What began as a technology trend is rapidly becoming a business reality. Across industries, semiconductor innovation is reshaping products, redefining competitive advantage and creating new opportunities for growth. In many ways, every industry is becoming a semiconductor industry, whether they recognize the shift or not.


As intelligence moves into the products and systems we use every day, AI is no longer confined to data centers and the cloud. It’s moving to the edge, embedded in vehicles, medical devices, industrial equipment, consumer products and critical infrastructure, including physical AI with robotics and smart drones. This shift is making the underlying silicon more important than ever.
